items.title: Mississauga marks 200th anniversary of one of Ontario's oldest log houses Aug. 8
items.summary: The Leslie Log House, built in 1826 by Scottish settlers, is one of Ontario’s oldest surviving log homes — and Mississauga is throwing it a free party. The Leslie Log House is operated by the Streetsville Historical Society. One of Ontario’s oldest surviving log homes is celebrating 200 years this weekend in Mississauga. The City of Mississauga and Streetsville Historical Society are hosting a public event to mark two centuries of the Leslie Log House on Aug. 8, according to a city press release. Built in 1826, the house was first occupied by John Leslie Sr. and his wife Esther Beattie Leslie, who arrived in Upper Canada (modern-day Ontario) from Scotland in 1824. m. Originally located near Derry Road and Mississauga Road in Meadowvale, the house was relocated to 4415 Mississauga Rd. in 1994 for preservation. It was designated under the Ontario Heritage Act for its architectural, historical and cultural significance.

items.title: Mississauga animal shelter full, drops adoption fees to $25 for dogs, cats
items.summary: The two-week event aims to reduce overcrowding at the city shelter. Mississauga Animal Services Shelter is also looking for some priority items and monetary donations. Mississauga Animal Services Shelter is offering adoption of cats and dogs for $25 to address overcrowding at the facility. The adoption event, Homeward Bound, runs from Aug. m. m. at their 735 Central Pky. W. location, according to a city press release. The facility has reached full capacity for dogs, which is why they’re offering a temporary promotional rate for dogs and cats of $25 plus HST and applicable municipal licensing fee for Mississauga residents. The reduced fee is a substantial drop from the standard adoption fee, which can cost approximately $280 plus taxes for dogs and puppies and up to $190 plus taxes for cats and kittens, according to the release. The two-week adoption event will allow the shelter to create necessary space for animals in need of shelter and care. The event is open to the public without appointments; however, visitors should be at least 18 years or older and should expect potential wait times, the city said in the statement.

items.title: House of the week: Upgraded home in family-friendly Mississauga neighbourhood
items.summary: This place: An upgraded home in a family-friendly Mississauga neighbourhood. Features: This upgraded home is located on a corner lot. A grand double-door entry opens to over 4,800 square feet of total living space that features hardwood floors throughout. The main level offers formal living and dining spaces, an office and a family room anchored by a fireplace. items.title: Three people charged after 19-year-old driver fatally shot by Toronto police
items.summary: MISSISSAUGA - Toronto police have charged three people, including a teenage girl, alleged to have been in a car with a 19-year-old man who was shot dead by an officer on Thursday. The Toronto Police Service logo is pictured in Toronto, Tuesday, March 12, 2024. THE CANADIAN PRESS/Arlyn McAdorey MISSISSAUGA - Toronto police have charged three people, including a teenage girl, alleged to have been in a car with a 19-year-old man who was shot dead by an officer on Thursday. Police say they were investigating a report of a person with a gun in The Esplanade area late Wednesday afternoon and tracked the suspect’s vehicle to Mississauga. They say officers tried to stop the car and its occupants, but the suspect tried to get away and the car struck a plainclothes officer. Ontario’s police watchdog, which launched an investigation into the incident, said Thursday that three unmarked police cruisers collided with the car shortly after midnight and one officer shot into the vehicle, hitting the 19-year-old driver. The Special Investigations Unit said the driver died at the scene and the three other people in the car were arrested. It said an officer was also taken to hospital to be treated for minor injuries. In a news release issued Friday, police say a 23-year-old from Toronto, a 19-year-old from Mississauga and a 17-year-old girl are each facing multiple firearms charges.

items.title: Halton, Peel communities warned of 'localized heavy rainfall' Friday
items.summary: Environment Canada and Credit Valley Conservation Authority issue weather statements. ” Environment Canada issued a widespread special weather statement Friday afternoon that included Peel and Halton regions, warning of possible “localized, heavy rainfall” exceeding 50 millimetres today (Friday, Aug. 7). “Scattered showers and thunderstorms are expected to develop this afternoon resulting in highly variable rainfall amounts. m. In response to the forecasted risk of thunderstorms and intense rainfall through Friday and Saturday, the Credit Valley Conservation Authority (CVC) has also issued a Flood Outlook statement, warning residents about the potential for localized flash flooding. The flood outlook remains in effect through Sunday as Environment Canada forecasts thunderstorms risk. CVC said that while flooding of the Credit River and its major tributaries is not expected, intense rainfall could lead to localized flash flooding and water pooling on roads, particularly in flood-prone and low-lying urban areas. “Urban streams and rivers may become dangerous, especially in the vicinity of culverts, bridges and dams. People are warned to stay away from all watercourses and to keep children and pets away,” CVC said in its advisory.

items.title: New details emerge after fatal police shooting in Mississauga as three face charges
items.summary: A Mississauga man is among three people facing firearms-related charges following a police investigation that ended with a fatal officer-involved shooting in Mississauga earlier this week. Toronto police announced Thursday that 19-year-old Kahiem Bailey-Whitfield of Mississauga, 23-year-old Naquon Laidley of Toronto, and a 17-year-old female youth have been charged following the investigation. The charges stem from an incident that began in Toronto and ended in Mississauga near The Collegeway and Winston Churchill Boulevard. According to Toronto police, officers received a report of a person with a gun near The Esplanade and Lower Jarvis Street in Toronto on Aug. m. Police said officers from 51 Division identified a suspect and vehicle, and plainclothes officers tracked the vehicle from Toronto to Mississauga. Police allege that when officers attempted to stop the vehicle in the area of The Collegeway and Winston Churchill Boulevard, the driver attempted to flee and struck a plainclothes officer. The events that followed, including the police shooting that left one man dead, are being investigated by Ontario’s Special Investigations Unit (SIU). Bailey-Whitfield faces multiple firearms charges, including two counts each of possessing a restricted or prohibited firearm without a licence and registration certificate, occupying a motor vehicle with a firearm, possessing a loaded regulated firearm, and possessing a prohibited or restricted weapon knowing there was no authority to do so.

items.title: One of Ontario’s biggest food festivals is back in Mississauga
items.summary: Barbecue lovers from across the GTA will be heading to Mississauga this weekend as one of Ontario’s biggest rib festivals returns for a second stop in the city this summer. Port Credit Ribfest X 2026 is taking over Memorial Park from Aug. 7 to 9, bringing award-winning rib teams, live entertainment, family activities and plenty of barbecue favourites to the waterfront community. Produced by Ontario Festival Group and presented by Gelateria Italiana, the three-day festival features some of North America’s top pitmasters serving up smoked ribs, pulled pork, brisket, BBQ chicken, smoked sausage and massive beef “Dino” ribs. Along with barbecue, visitors can sample a variety of festival favourites, including bloomin’ onions, roasted corn, poutine, cold beverages and plenty of sweet treats. Food vendors include Gelateria Italiana, Alabama Lemonade, Billy Bob’s Bloomin’ Onions, Pineapple Queen, Chocolate N Strawberries, Heavenly Pop’T, Ontario Corn Roasters, Pappy’s Olde Fashion Soda Pop, Mister Treats, BeaverTails, Tiny Tom Donuts and Slushy Bear. Beyond the food, organizers have planned a full weekend of entertainment and activities, including live music, a marketplace, artisan vendors, carnival games, a midway, face painting and a Kids Zone. The entertainment lineup includes tribute performances and local bands throughout the weekend. Friday’s lineup features Ida-Maria, Dingo, Pink Leather Jackets and Fiddlestix.

items.title: Credit Valley Conservation Warns of Dangerous Urban Streams as Storms Soak the Region Through Saturday
items.summary: According to INsauga, Credit Valley Conservation issued a flood outlook statement Thursday covering Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon that remains in effect through Sunday. The agency says thunderstorms carrying peak rainfall of 30 to 40 millimetres per hour are possible both Friday and Saturday, with Environment and Climate Change Canada forecasting localized storms across the entire Credit River watershed starting Friday morning and continuing into Saturday evening. CVC reports the upper and middle sections of the watershed had already picked up roughly 20 to 30 millimetres of localized rainfall as of Thursday evening. While the agency says it does not expect the Credit River or its major tributaries to flood outright, it is warning of possible localized flash flooding and water pooling on roads and in low-lying urban areas. CVC cautions that urban streams and rivers can become especially dangerous near culverts, bridges and dams during heavy rain events. Residents are being told to stay away from all watercourses and to keep children and pets clear of moving water through the weekend.

items.title: City launches $25 adoption event as animal shelter reaches capacity
items.summary: The Homeward Bound adoption event offers $25 adoption fees for all dogs and cats from August 8 to 22. Are you looking to add a furry family member to your home? Now is the perfect time to adopt one. The Mississauga Animal Services Shelter is asking residents to help shelter animals find loving homes during the Homeward Bound adoption event. With the shelter reaching capacity for dogs, every adoption helps create space for other animals in need. From August 8 to 22, all dogs and cats at the shelter can be adopted for just $25, plus HST and any applicable pet licence fees for Mississauga residents. This reduced adoption fee offers significant savings compared to regular fees, which are typically $280 plus HST for dogs and puppies and up to $190 plus HST for cats and kittens.
